newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya shilling stronger against the dollar.
newsitem.headline: Kenya shilling stronger against the dollar.

text.p: The Kenyan shilling strengthened versus the dollar on Tuesday in an active market, dealers said.
The Central Bank of Kenya (CBK) posted a shilling mean rate of 56.35 against the dollar from 56.47 on Monday. On the pound, it was posted at an average of 87.80 from 87.92 on Monday.

"The market opened the week with little interest from both importers and exporters," a dealer said. "The opening levels were 56.35/45 for the dollar which persisted most of the day despite some attempts by some players to bid to buy the dollar lower.
Another dealer added: "However, at the close of day, the shilling gave in to pressure from a large buy order to close a touch weaker at 56.40/45."
"Sentiment continues to point towards a stronger shilling as supply still outstrips demand in the absence of factors to influence market direction," she said.
Dealers said overnight money market rates maintained Friday's average of 20 percent levels in the wake of depressed liquidity.
